Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom

Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (CISO, Oakmont), Marcus Lee (Security Manager, Oakmont), Dr. Anya Patel (CTO, Oakmont)

Encryption at rest/in-transit and KMS/HSM integration
Data residency and private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Samir on the account team, Lena's our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Karen: Hi all, Karen Liu, CISO at Oakmont. We're mainly interested in SOC 2 and ISO posture and how Redwood fits into our control scope.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus here, security ops — I'll be digging into logs and KMS details.
[00:20] Lena: Great. Agenda — we'll walk through our SOC 2/ISO evidence, trust center, controls mapping approach, then cover RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption and KMS, and data residency options.
[00:30] Samir: Quick note — apologies if audio weirdness, we're on a new laptop.
[00:34] Karen: No worries. We did review the compliance sheet you sent but want to be clear about shared responsibility, what we need from Redwood, and what remains on Oakmont.
[00:43] Lena: Absolutely. At a high level Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the hosted service and we have ISO 27001 scope for the control plane. We can share the Type II report under NDA and provide an ISO certificate link; both are live.
[00:55] Karen: Is the scope full production? Are there carve-outs we should be aware of?
[01:00] Lena: There are standard carve-outs — third-party infrastructure providers like cloud infra are called out. We'll call them out in the controls mapping. For the most part the controls cover our control plane and hosted runtime; dedicated/private deployments have slightly different coverage and we document that.
[01:15] Marcus: Regarding audit logs — we need to know retention, export format, and whether logs include token-level activity and request-level metadata.
[01:25] Lena: Logs include request timestamps, route/model, request ID, redacted user input by default unless customers enable content retention, and response latencies. We support log export to S3 or syslog; retention configurable by plan but default is 90 days for hosted, longer for enterprise plans.
[01:40] Marcus: Okay, can retention be extended to 365 days in hosted?
[01:45] Samir: Yes, that's part of the enterprise add-on, we can set retention to 1 year and provide a searchable export.
[01:52] Karen: How about immutable audit trail for compliance? We need tamper-evident logs for certain controls.
[01:58] Lena: We offer write-once storage and integration with customer-managed logging sinks which you can put behind WORM policies. We also provide signed log digests for an extra assurance layer.
[02:10] Marcus: Good, that helps. On SSO — we use SAML 2.0, Okta for identity. How's Redwood's integration?
[02:16] Lena: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for user sync, RBAC with custom roles and least-privilege controls. We can do SCIM push to manage groups and map to roles.
[02:27] Karen: Can role changes be audited? We need an audit trail when admin privileges are assigned.
[02:33] Lena: Yes, role assignment events are recorded and appear in the admin audit log with timestamp and actor.
[02:38] Dr. Anya: Wanted to ask about key management — we currently use AWS KMS. Does Redwood allow customer-managed keys?
[02:44] Lena: For Private/VPC deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own), and for the hosted API we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default; we also support customer-managed keys via an HSM/KMS integration on enterprise plans.
[02:58] Samir: To add — if you require a dedicated HSM or FIPS-validated HSM, we can discuss options for private deployments or dedicated capacity with KMS integration.
[03:08] Marcus: Key rotation policies — do you support automatic rotation and also a way to rotate without downtime?
[03:13] Lena: Yes, we support key rotation with automatic re-encryption and a zero-downtime rollover process for active keys. We also provide audit logs for key usage and rotation events.
[03:24] Karen: About controls mapping — we need a mapping table that ties your SOC/ISO controls to our internal control IDs and evidence artifacts.
[03:31] Samir: We'll provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to Oakmont controls, expected evidence, and the location (trust center/doc link). Lena will own that deliverable.
[03:40] Karen: Perfect. Trust Center — can we get read-only access to the trust center and evidence repository? We may request pen test reports and third-party attestation docs.
[03:49] Samir: Yes, we can provision a read-only trust center link and send over the process for requesting restricted documents under NDA.
[03:56] Marcus: Pen test frequency? Are those internal or third-party?
[03:59] Lena: Annual third-party pen tests with remediation tracking; high-severity findings are prioritized. We can share the executive summary and remediation timeline. Full reports may require a bilateral NDA.
[04:12] Karen: Data residency — we operate in multiple states and some PHI flows. For PHI, we need to know whether Redwood persists raw inputs, and if so, where.
[04:23] Lena: Default hosted mode redacts and does not persist customer inputs unless you opt-in to retention for debugging. For PHI-heavy workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with regional placement; we also have a data residency add-on to pin data to a region.
[04:39] Dr. Anya: If we go with dedicated capacity in our VPC, can we maintain encryption keys and ensure logs never leave our environment?
[04:46] Lena: Yes, with private deployments you can bring your own keys and configure log sinks to your VPC so logs stay within your environment.
[04:54] Marcus: Is there any customer data in backups that might go cross-region?
[04:58] Lena: Backups for the hosted service are encrypted and may be stored in multiple regions for DR; we document region storage in the trust center. For dedicated/private we can customize backup policies to satisfy residency requirements.
[05:10] Karen: About ISO 27001 — do you map which Annex A controls are in scope?
[05:15] Lena: Yes, our ISO scope includes Annex A mappings and we will include that in the controls mapping file.
[05:22] Samir: I'll make sure the artifacts we share include the ISO certificate scan and the scope document.
[05:28] Karen: One more — incident response. What's the SLA and notification process if there's a security incident?
[05:33] Lena: We have an incident response runbook, notify customers within our SLA window depending on severity (e.g., initial notification within 4 hours for critical incidents), and provide post-incident reports and remediation timelines. Enterprise customers can get additional SLAs and direct pager contact.
[05:47] Marcus: That aligns with our expectations. A couple of technical follow-ups we want in the KMS deep dive: support for key access logs, ability to rotate provider, and performance impact on latency for encryption operations.
[05:59] Lena: Noted. We'll prepare data points and some benchmark numbers for the deep dive.
[06:05] Karen: For compliance sign-off we may need a statement of applicability showing control ownership. Can you provide which controls are 'redwood-owned' vs 'customer-owned' for hybrid setups?
[06:15] Samir: Yes, the controls mapping will include ownership columns — redwood, customer, or shared, with suggested evidence sources.
[06:23] Dr. Anya: Anything else we should know about third-party subservice orgs?
[06:27] Lena: We list key subservice providers in the report. For example our cloud infra provider and certain telemetry vendors are identified and covered under our vendor management program.
[06:36] Karen: Thanks. Let's recap next steps. Samir to send SOC report and trust center link, Lena to send controls mapping and SSO checklist, and we will schedule KMS deep dive.
[06:47] Samir: Correct. I'll share the SOC 2 Type II and the trust center invite by Friday.
[06:52] Lena: I'll put together the mapping and SAML/SCIM checklist and share a calendar invite for the KMS deep dive.
[06:59] Marcus: I'll gather our KMS config and share before the deep dive.
[07:03] Karen: OK sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:06] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the artifacts. End.

Note: Transcript has typical speech disfluencies and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., some product names spelled differently); timestamps are approximate.
